subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: If A and B are independent events with P(A) = 0.2, P(B) = 0.5, find (i) P(A|B) (ii) P(B|A) (iii) P(A ∩ B) (iv) P(A ∪ B).

recall_prompt: Say how you would find the four quantities for independent events with P(A) = 0.2 and P(B) = 0.5 — the rule each part uses and the number.
insider_note: Parts (i) and (ii) are one line each: for independent events a condition changes nothing. The only computation is part (iv).

steps.label: A and B are independent
steps.margin_note: No mark of its own. Write the given values and the word "independent" — it is the reason behind parts (i), (ii) and (iii).

recall.must_convey: That A and B are independent with P(A) = 0.2 and P(B) = 0.5.
accept: A and B are independent with P A point two and P B point five
the events are independent, point two and point five
independent events, P of A is 0.2 and P of B is 0.5
A B independent, P A 0.2, P B 0.5 ani given

steps.why: Independence is what makes each conditional probability equal the plain one and the intersection a product.
common_mistakes: Not writing "independent" and then using the rules with no reason.

steps.label: (i) P(A|B)

recall.must_convey: That for independent events P(A|B) = P(A) = 0.2.
accept: P of A given B equals P of A which is point two
independent so A given B is just P A, 0.2
A given B is point two
independent kabatti P A given B ante P A, 0.2

steps.why: Knowing B happened does not change the chance of A when the events are independent.

steps.label: (ii) P(B|A)

recall.must_convey: That for independent events P(B|A) = P(B) = 0.5.
accept: P of B given A equals P of B which is point five
independent so B given A is just P B, 0.5
B given A is half
independent kabatti P B given A ante P B, 0.5

steps.why: Same reason as part (i) with the roles swapped.

steps.label: (iii) P(A ∩ B)

accept: P of A intersection B is P A times P B which is point one
independent so multiply point two by point five to get 0.1
the intersection is the product 0.1
independent kabatti P A into P B, 0.1

steps.why: P(A ∩ B) = P(A)·P(B) is the definition of independence.

steps.label: (iv) P(A ∪ B)

lines.text: (iv) P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B)

accept: P of A union B is P A plus P B minus P A intersection B which is point six
addition theorem 0.2 plus 0.5 minus 0.1 equals 0.6
the union is point six
addition theorem tho 0.2 plus 0.5 minus 0.1 ante 0.6

steps.why: The union subtracts the overlap once; the overlap is the product found in part (iii).
common_mistakes: Writing P(A ∪ B) = 0.7, the plain sum.
